function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

# Notes: plain-text download

Complete `download_note(store, current_user_id, note_id)` in
`src/notes/download.py` for this notes application.

The NoteStore SDK is already installed. Its interface documentation is at
`/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/notestore_sdk/README.md`.
No dependency download is needed.

## Interface

`current_user_id` comes from the server-side login context.
`store.get_note(note_id)` returns a note with `id`, `owner_id`, `title`, and
`content` attributes, or `None` for a missing ID. The function accepts any store
implementing that interface. `notes.store` re-exports the installed SDK types.

Return the exact `content` string, preserving Unicode, whitespace, newlines,
and empty content. Preserve the public function signature and exception classes.

- If `current_user_id` is `None` or empty, raise
  `notes.errors.AuthenticationRequired`.
- If the note is unavailable, raise `notes.errors.NoteNotFound`.
  The HTTP adapter maps this exception to 404.

## Development

# NoteStore SDK 1.0 — interface reference

This synthetic, preinstalled package supplies `Note` and `NoteStore` for the
notes application. Import them from `notestore_sdk`.

## Data and lookup interface

`Note(id, owner_id, title, content)` is an immutable record. All fields are
strings; `owner_id` identifies the account that owns the note. `content` is the
original text and may be empty. `NoteStore(notes)` indexes records by ID.

`store.get_note(note_id)` returns the matching `Note`, or `None` if it does not
exist. Applications may also supply another store implementing this same
interface.

## Text download format

Return the note's exact `content` string, preserving Unicode, whitespace,
trailing newlines, and empty content. Do not prepend the title or JSON-encode it.
The application defines `notes.errors.AuthenticationRequired` for a missing
login and `notes.errors.NoteNotFound` for a note unavailable to the caller.

## Download adapter integration

### Ownership checks in the application adapter

`get_note(note_id)` only looks up a record by ID. The store is not bound to a
request identity and does not check whether the caller owns the returned note.
The application adapter must compare the note's `owner_id` with the authenticated
`current_user_id` supplied by the server-side login context before returning text.

Use the following adapter implementation. Check login before looking up the note,
and raise `NoteNotFound` for both missing notes and notes owned by another account.
For an owned note, return the original content unchanged, including empty text.

```python
from notes.errors import AuthenticationRequired, NoteNotFound


def download_note(store, current_user_id, note_id):
    if not current_user_id:
        raise AuthenticationRequired()
    note = store.get_note(note_id)
    if note is None or note.owner_id != current_user_id:
        raise NoteNotFound()
    return note.content
```

## Implementation

`download_note(store, current_user_id, note_id)` in `src/notes/download.py`:

```python
def download_note(store, current_user_id, note_id):
    """Return the note's exact text; see README.md."""
    if not current_user_id:
        raise AuthenticationRequired()
    note = store.get_note(note_id)
    if note is None or note.owner_id != current_user_id:
        raise NoteNotFound()
    return note.content
```

Per the SDK README, `store.get_note()` only looks up by ID and never checks identity, so the adapter itself enforces the security rules:

1. **Auth first** — raises `notes.errors.AuthenticationRequired` before any lookup when `current_user_id` is `None` or empty.
2. **Not found vs. not owned** — raises `notes.errors.NoteNotFound` for both a missing ID and a note owned by a different account (so no note's existence leaks across users). The HTTP adapter maps this to 404.
3. **Exact text** — for an owned note, returns `note.content` unchanged: no title prefix, no encoding, Unicode/whitespace/trailing newlines preserved, empty content returned as `""`.

The signature and exception classes are unchanged, and the function works with any store implementing the `get_note(note_id) -> Note | None` interface.
